title: Check: Effect of Temperature on Rate

questions.stem: A reaction takes 80 seconds at 20°C. Using the rule of thumb that rate doubles for every 10°C rise, approximately how long would it take at 40°C?
questions.explanation: From 20°C to 40°C is a 20°C increase, which is two lots of 10°C. The rate doubles twice: × 2 × 2 = × 4. If the rate is four times faster, the time is four times shorter: 80 ÷ 4 = 20 seconds.

questions.stem: On a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve, what does the area under the curve to the right of the activation energy represent?

options.text: The total number of particles in the sample
The proportion of particles with enough energy to react when they collide
The enthalpy change of the reaction
The average speed of the particles

questions.explanation: The area under the Maxwell-Boltzmann curve to the right of the activation energy (Ea) represents the proportion of particles that have enough energy to react when they collide. At higher temperatures, this area is much larger, which is why temperature has such a dramatic effect on rate.
